comparison: Perfect agreement on genetic evidence (C1, C26, C38-C46). Both OpenEval and all three peer reviewers affirm CCDC146 mutations as a novel cause of male infertility with solid evidence from WES, validation, pathogenicity prediction, and mouse models.

Strong agreement on mouse KO model findings (C4-C6, C47-C54). Both evaluations confirm the model recapitulates human phenotype with quantitative fertility, sperm, and morphology data. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the mouse model as proving causative role.

Agreement on somatic cell localization (C2, C57-C64). Both evaluations support immunofluorescence findings in HEK-293T and HFF cells showing localization to microtubule-organizing structures. Peer reviewers accept these findings without critique.

Agreement on flagellar localization (C8-C9, C65, C67, C72, C76, C80-C83, C120, C123-C128, C142). Both evaluations support Western blot, IF, and expansion microscopy data showing association with microtubule doublets. Peer reviewers affirm CCDC146 as microtubule-associated protein.

Agreement on uncertainty of MIP localization (C10, C84-C87, C129-C132). Both OpenEval and Reviewer 3 explicitly acknowledge the evidence is suggestive but not definitive. OpenEval cites C132 stating more experiments needed; Reviewer 3 states data 'indicate, but do not prove beyond any doubt' MIP classification.

Agreement on timing of defects during spermatogenesis (C167-C169). Both evaluations support RT-PCR and histological data showing CCDC146 is required specifically for late spermiogenesis with defects appearing from elongation onset. Peer reviewers accept timing findings as part of comprehensive phenotypic analysis.

Agreement on HTCA defects (C11, C88-C95). Both evaluations support scanning EM, IF, and TEM data showing centriole separation, displacement, and absence of emerging microtubules. Reviewer 3 explicitly affirms 'centrioles...are defective when CCDC146 is absent.'

Agreement on manchette defects (C96-C104, C173). Both evaluations support IF and TEM data showing defective manchette organization, elongated manchettes with quantitative measurements, and mislocalized perinuclear ring. Reviewer 3 explicitly states 'sperm manchette...are defective when CCDC146 is absent.'

Agreement on axoneme and dense fiber defects (C105-C107). Both evaluations support TEM data showing axoneme disorganization and fragmented dense fibers. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of comprehensive phenotypic characterization of microtubule-based organelle defects.

Agreement on nuclear and acrosomal abnormalities (C108-C111). Both evaluations support TEM data showing nuclear defects during elongation, bilobed nuclei with vacuoles, and severe acrosome deformations. Peer reviewers accept these as part of the comprehensive phenotypic analysis.

Agreement on CCDC146 as MAP (C3, C141). Both evaluations support classification as microtubule-associated protein based on consistent localization to microtubule structures across cell types. Reviewer 3 explicitly states 'Their data show that CCDC146 is a microtubule-associated protein' and Reviewer 2 describes it as 'a centriole and microtubule-associated protein.'

Agreement on tissue-specific function (C139, C162). Both evaluations note CCDC146 is dispensable outside spermatogenesis based on viable, fertile KO females and absence of other phenotypes. Reviewer 3 states 'animals develop no other obvious pathologies, thus underpinning the specific role of CCDC146 in male fertility.'

OpenEval evaluates quality control for antibody specificity (C133-C138), identifying non-specific acrosomal and midpiece staining. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though Reviewer 2 generally states 'the authors' claims are well supported by the biochemical and imaging approaches.'

OpenEval evaluates literature context on multiple localization patterns (C143-C151), noting 80% of centrosomal proteins show multiple localizations with specific examples. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates sequence analysis findings (C152-C157) identifying PF05557 motif and coiled-coil domains. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates evolutionary conservation evidence (C158-C161) comparing to MBO2 in Chlamydomonas. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates comparison to Katanin80 and WDR62 KO models as UNCERTAIN (C171-C178), noting speculation about molecular mechanisms. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers generally praise the comprehensive phenotypic analysis.
OpenEval evaluates distinction from acephalic syndrome (C181-C185) based on supernumerary centrioles without decapitation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates reconciliation with proteomics data (C119-C122), explaining apparent centrosomal localization in prior studies via co-purification due to poor solubility. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates cohort context (C24-C25) showing 50% of MMAF patients lack molecular diagnosis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval rates speculation about cancer risk as UNCERTAIN (C163-C166), noting no current phenotype but citing thyroid cancer downregulation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates synthesis of manchette-centriole relationship literature (C186-C190). No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates background information on male infertility (C12-C23) with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers focus on novel findings rather than background claims.
OpenEval evaluates background on centrosomal proteins and MMAF genetics (C27-C37, C112). No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates discussion points on MMAF genetics and clinical implications (C113, C115-C118). No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
